main_text.p: fuae totiusq; posteritatis consulere fata-gebat, ea ipsa ratione ignominiam & ⸗ πολισθέμιν eidem accersere diceretur. Certum autem est, iusticia stabiliri thronum, iniusticia subuerti. Itaque Rex iniuste a-gens, pessime sibi suisq; consulebat.

2. Quòd excidisset populos multos. Reuocat Dominus Tyranno in memo-riam crudelitatem, quâ erga multas gen-tes, quas bellis deuicerat, declarârat. Etsi autem hoc genus hominum adeò asperi esse solent monitoribus suis, ut nemo liberè eos obiurgare audet: Deus tamen ἀκριβῶς nouit, qua ratione exsuscitanda sit conscientia, sic ut mille testium instar sit, & ut Tyrannos horribiliter excarnificet: ut testatur exempla Neronis, qui sibi terra dehiscente absorberi & exstingui uisus est, & multorum aliorum.

3. Quòd in animam suam peccasset. Vt qui scortatur, in proprium corpus peccat: 1. Cor. 6. 18. sic qui in Deum & homines iniurius est, in suam ipsius animam peccat: ei enim exitiû & poenas aeternas ac-cersit.
Iam vero, ut ad usum nostrum ista transfe-ramus, tria nobis summo studio cauen-da sunt.

page.notes: Greek words in the text are printed in Greek letters; the Greek on the line "ea ipsa ratione ignominiam" and the word after "Deus tamen" are set in Greek type and were read approximately: "πολισθέμιν" and "ἀκριβῶς" are doubtful and should be checked against the scan. Likely [?] candidates: the Greek after "&" in line 3 of the first paragraph. The fragment "1. Ne" at the foot is incomplete, the text continues on the next page. Some letters are blurred in the first lines (e.g. "suisq;"); the reading is uncertain. The leading line of the page is a running head, not text.
